stories.title: YouTube will count a view as soon as a video starts playing
stories.summary: YouTube is changing its view-counting methodology so that a view registers the moment a video begins playing, rather than requiring a longer watch threshold. The change is expected to take effect in the near term and will likely push publicly displayed view counts higher across the platform.
stories.whyItMatters: View counts are a core currency for creators, advertisers, and platform bragging rights, so a methodology change that inflates them affects how success is measured across the video industry.
whatToWatch: Whether YouTube publishes exact criteria for the new counting standard
How advertisers and creators react to inflated public numbers
Whether other video platforms follow with similar changes
questions: Will YouTube distinguish publicly displayed counts from the metrics used for ad billing and creator payouts?
How much will average view counts rise across the platform?

stories.title: Apple ordered to stop steering iPhone and iPad users away from third-party apps
stories.summary: Apple has been ordered to stop using its personal data collection prompts to discourage users from choosing third-party apps over its own, according to reports. The order targets how Apple's in-device prompts are worded and presented, which critics say nudged users toward Apple's own apps and services.
stories.whyItMatters: The ruling adds to mounting regulatory pressure on Apple's control over app choice and default settings on its devices, a fight with implications for competition across mobile software.
whatToWatch: How Apple redesigns its data-collection prompts in response
Whether the order applies broadly across iPhone and iPad or to specific markets
Any Apple appeal or compliance timeline
questions: Which regulator issued the order, and in which jurisdiction does it apply?
Will Apple make the same changes globally or only where required?

stories.title: Groq raises $350M as it pivots from AI chips to 'neocloud' services
stories.summary: AI chipmaker Groq has raised $350 million to support a strategic shift from selling AI inference chips toward operating as a 'neocloud' — a cloud provider built around its own AI hardware. The funding underscores Groq's bet that renting out compute capacity, rather than just chip sales, is the bigger opportunity.
stories.whyItMatters: The move reflects a broader trend of AI chip startups repositioning as infrastructure providers to compete with Nvidia and hyperscalers for a slice of surging AI compute demand.
whatToWatch: How Groq scales its neocloud offering and who its early customers are
Whether other AI chip startups follow with similar cloud pivots

questions: Who led this funding round and at what valuation?

stories.title: Nvidia invests $1.5B in SoftBank-backed data center developer tied to OpenAI project
stories.summary: Nvidia is investing $1.5 billion in a data center developer backed by SoftBank that is involved in building infrastructure for an OpenAI-linked project. The investment deepens ties between Nvidia, SoftBank, and OpenAI as the three continue to expand AI infrastructure buildout.
stories.whyItMatters: Nvidia's direct stake in AI data center development, rather than just chip sales, shows how deeply the chipmaker is embedding itself across the AI infrastructure supply chain that underpins the industry's growth.

stories.whyItMatters: Early fire detection technology has growing relevance as climate-driven wildfire and industrial fire risks push demand for faster, tech-based prevention tools.

stories.title: AI automation startup Relay shuts down; staff move to Google's Chrome team
stories.summary: AI automation startup Relay has shut down, with its staff joining Google's Chrome team. The shutdown adds to a pattern of AI startups closing and being absorbed by larger tech companies, often in acquihire-style arrangements.
stories.whyItMatters: The deal reflects how big platforms like Google continue to absorb AI talent from startups that can't sustain independent growth, consolidating expertise inside a handful of major players.
whatToWatch: What Relay's team will work on within Chrome
Whether more AI automation startups face similar shutdowns

stories.title: Investigators report 'unprecedented' number of Apple users hit by spyware alerts
stories.summary: Security investigators say an unusually large number of Apple device users recently received alerts warning they may have been targeted by spyware. The scale of the alert wave is being described as unprecedented compared to past notifications of this kind.
stories.whyItMatters: A spike in spyware targeting notifications signals either a broader surveillance campaign or a change in detection, both significant for how vulnerable high-value iPhone users are to state-linked or commercial spyware.

stories.title: Flock's camera network loses value as Wisconsin cities pull out
stories.summary: Multiple Wisconsin cities are dropping Flock Safety's shared surveillance camera network, reducing the network's overall coverage and value. Flock's system relies on many connected municipalities to be effective, so departures weaken the network for those that remain.
stories.whyItMatters: The pullback highlights growing local pushback against police surveillance camera networks and could pressure Flock's business model, which depends on broad municipal participation.
whatToWatch: Whether more cities beyond Wisconsin follow suit
Flock's response to the departures
Any local policy debates driving the decisions
questions: What specifically prompted these Wisconsin cities to leave the network?

stories.title: Supreme Court rejects Verizon's bid to recover $47 million FCC fine
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has declined Verizon's request to overturn or refund a $47 million fine imposed by the FCC. The decision leaves the fine in place, closing off Verizon's path to recovering the money through the courts.
stories.whyItMatters: The ruling reinforces the FCC's authority to levy and defend fines against major telecom carriers, a precedent relevant to future regulatory enforcement in the industry.
